idiom_name: NSCache (auto-evicting, thread-safe) or a Dictionary with an explicit policy; URLCache for HTTP
implementation_notes: Foundation ships the cache: NSCache is a thread-safe key-value store that evicts automatically under memory pressure, with countLimit/totalCostLimit and a per-entry cost, and it is the platform answer for in-memory caching of recomputable objects. For value-typed, deterministic caches the idiom is a wrapper struct around Dictionary plus timestamps and an explicit bound, exploiting Swift's copy-on-write (copies are cheap until mutation). HTTP responses have a dedicated cache: URLCache with URLSession honours response headers through HTTPURLResponse, giving TTL and revalidation without application code. The classic hand-written store is justified only when NSCache's eviction policy is too coarse or its Objective-C object model is unsuitable.
pitfalls: NSCache cannot be enumerated or inspected: there is no size, no keys view and no selective invalidation beyond removing individual keys, so the authority must live elsewhere.
Eviction happens under memory pressure and is not deterministic - never store the only copy of data that cannot be recomputed.
Dictionary is a value type: storing large structs copies on write, so cache reference types or wrap payloads in a class/box when the copy cost matters.
URLCache revalidation follows server headers; setting it up without honouring Cache-Control/ETag gives stale or duplicated fetches rather than caching.
